title: 10. NLP, Transformers & LLMs: Logistic Regression for Text Classification
summary: Goal: Master logistic regression for binary and multi-class text classification.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: **Goal**: Master logistic regression for binary and multi-class text classification.

sections.title: Why Logistic Regression for Text?
sections.body:
### Advantages
```
✓ Fast to train (even with millions of features)
✓ Interpretable (feature weights)
✓ Works well with TF-IDF
✓ Probabilistic output (confidence scores)
✓ Handles high-dimensional sparse data
✓ Regularization prevents overfitting
```

### When to Use
```
✓ Sentiment analysis
✓ Spam detection
✓ Topic classification
✓ Binary/multi-class problems
✓ Need interpretability
```

sections.title: Quick Math Refresher
sections.body:
### Binary Logistic Regression

**Linear combination**:
$$
z = w_0 + w_1 x_1 + w_2 x_2 + \ldots + w_n x_n = w^T x
$$

**Sigmoid function** (squashes to [0, 1]):
$$
\sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}}
$$

**Prediction**:
$$
P(y=1|x) = \sigma(w^T x)
$$

```
If P(y=1|x) > 0.5 → Predict class 1
If P(y=1|x) ≤ 0.5 → Predict class 0
```

### Visualization
```
z (score):  -∞  -4  -2   0   2   4   ∞
            │   │   │   │   │   │   │
σ(z):       0  0.02 0.12 0.5 0.88 0.98 1
            └───────┴────┴───┴────┴───┘
         Class 0      Uncertain    Class 1
```

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score, GridSearchCV
from sklearn.metrics import (
    classification_report, confusion_matrix, roc_curve, auc, 
    precision_recall_curve, average_precision_score
)
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

sns.set_style('whitegrid')
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (12, 6)

# For reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)
```

sections.title: Dataset: Movie Reviews (Sentiment Analysis)
sections.body:
```python
# Sample movie reviews
reviews = [
    # Positive reviews
    "This movie was absolutely fantastic! Great acting and amazing story.",
    "Loved every minute of it. Best film I've seen this year!",
    "Brilliant performance by the lead actor. Highly recommended!",
    "Outstanding cinematography and beautiful soundtrack. A masterpiece!",
    "Incredible movie! The plot twists kept me engaged throughout.",
    "Exceptional film with great character development and pacing.",
    "Absolutely wonderful! This is cinema at its finest.",
    "Superb direction and excellent script. Five stars!",
    "A must-watch! The performances were phenomenal.",
    "Thoroughly enjoyed it. One of the best movies of the decade.",
    # Negative reviews
    "Terrible movie. Waste of time and money.",
    "Boring and predictable. Very disappointed with this film.",
    "Poor acting and weak storyline. Would not recommend.",
    "Awful cinematography and confusing plot. Complete disaster.",
    "One of the worst movies I've ever seen. Terrible script.",
    "Disappointing film with bad pacing and mediocre performances.",
    "Horrible movie. I want my money back!",
    "Dull and uninspiring. The plot made no sense at all.",
    "Extremely boring. I fell asleep halfway through.",
    "Poorly directed and badly written. Complete waste of time.",
] * 10  # Replicate for better training

sentiments = ([1] * 10 + [0] * 10) * 10  # 1=positive, 0=negative

print(f"📊 Dataset: {len(reviews)} reviews")
print(f"   Positive: {sum(sentiments)} ({sum(sentiments)/len(sentiments)*100:.0f}%)")
print(f"   Negative: {len(sentiments) - sum(sentiments)} ({(len(sentiments) - sum(sentiments))/len(sentiments)*100:.0f}%)")
print()
print("Sample reviews:")
for i in range(4):
    label = "POSITIVE" if sentiments[i] == 1 else "NEGATIVE"
    print(f"  [{label}] {reviews[i]}")
```

sections.title: Step 1: Train-Test Split
sections.body:
```python
# Split data
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    reviews, sentiments, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=sentiments
)

print("📊 Data Split:")
print(f"   Training set: {len(X_train)} reviews")
print(f"   Test set:     {len(X_test)} reviews")
print()
print(f"   Training positive: {sum(y_train)} ({sum(y_train)/len(y_train)*100:.0f}%)")
print(f"   Test positive:     {sum(y_test)} ({sum(y_test)/len(y_test)*100:.0f}%)")
```

sections.title: Step 2: Create TF-IDF Features
sections.body:
```python
# Create TF-IDF vectorizer
vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(
    max_features=500,
    min_df=2,
    max_df=0.8,
    stop_words='english',
    ngram_range=(1, 2)
)

# Transform training and test data
X_train_tfidf = vectorizer.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test_tfidf = vectorizer.transform(X_test)

print("📊 TF-IDF Feature Matrix:")
print(f"   Training shape: {X_train_tfidf.shape}")
print(f"   Test shape:     {X_test_tfidf.shape}")
print(f"   Vocabulary size: {len(vectorizer.get_feature_names_out())}")
print(f"   Sparsity: {(1 - X_train_tfidf.nnz / (X_train_tfidf.shape[0] * X_train_tfidf.shape[1])):.2%}")
```

sections.title: Step 3: Train Logistic Regression
sections.body:
```python
# Train logistic regression
lr_model = LogisticRegression(
    random_state=42,
    max_iter=1000,
    C=1.0  # Regularization strength (smaller = stronger)
)

lr_model.fit(X_train_tfidf, y_train)

# Predictions
y_pred = lr_model.predict(X_test_tfidf)
y_pred_proba = lr_model.predict_proba(X_test_tfidf)[:, 1]

# Accuracy
train_accuracy = lr_model.score(X_train_tfidf, y_train)
test_accuracy = lr_model.score(X_test_tfidf, y_test)

print("🎯 Model Performance:")
print(f"   Training accuracy: {train_accuracy:.3f}")
print(f"   Test accuracy:     {test_accuracy:.3f}")
```

sections.title: Step 4: Detailed Evaluation
sections.body:
```python
# Classification report
print("📋 Classification Report:")
print()
print(classification_report(
    y_test, y_pred,
    target_names=['Negative', 'Positive'],
    digits=3
))
```

```python
# Confusion matrix
cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred)

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt='d', cmap='Blues', 
            xticklabels=['Negative', 'Positive'],
            yticklabels=['Negative', 'Positive'],
            cbar_kws={'label': 'Count'})
plt.ylabel('True Label')
plt.xlabel('Predicted Label')
plt.title('Confusion Matrix: Sentiment Classification')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("\n💡 Confusion Matrix Interpretation:")
print(f"   True Negatives (TN):  {cm[0, 0]} - Correctly identified negative reviews")
print(f"   False Positives (FP): {cm[0, 1]} - Negative reviews classified as positive")
print(f"   False Negatives (FN): {cm[1, 0]} - Positive reviews classified as negative")
print(f"   True Positives (TP):  {cm[1, 1]} - Correctly identified positive reviews")
```

sections.title: ROC Curve and AUC
sections.body:
```python
# Calculate ROC curve
fpr, tpr, thresholds = roc_curve(y_test, y_pred_proba)
roc_auc = auc(fpr, tpr)

# Plot ROC curve
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
plt.plot(fpr, tpr, color='darkorange', lw=2, 
         label=f'ROC curve (AUC = {roc_auc:.3f})')
plt.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], color='navy', lw=2, linestyle='--', 
         label='Random classifier')
plt.xlim([0.0, 1.0])
plt.ylim([0.0, 1.05])
plt.xlabel('False Positive Rate')
plt.ylabel('True Positive Rate')
plt.title('Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Curve')
plt.legend(loc='lower right')
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("\n📊 ROC-AUC Interpretation:")
print(f"   AUC = {roc_auc:.3f}")
print("   • 1.0 = Perfect classifier")
print("   • 0.5 = Random guessing")
print("   • Higher = Better!")
```

sections.title: Precision-Recall Curve
sections.body:
```python
# Calculate precision-recall curve
precision, recall, pr_thresholds = precision_recall_curve(y_test, y_pred_proba)
avg_precision = average_precision_score(y_test, y_pred_proba)

# Plot precision-recall curve
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
plt.plot(recall, precision, color='purple', lw=2,
         label=f'PR curve (AP = {avg_precision:.3f})')
plt.xlabel('Recall')
plt.ylabel('Precision')
plt.title('Precision-Recall Curve')
plt.legend(loc='lower left')
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.xlim([0.0, 1.0])
plt.ylim([0.0, 1.05])
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("\n📊 Precision-Recall Trade-off:")
print("   • High precision → Few false positives")
print("   • High recall → Few false negatives")
print("   • Usually can't maximize both!")
```

sections.title: Feature Importance: Most Predictive Words
sections.body:
```python
# Get feature names and coefficients
feature_names = vectorizer.get_feature_names_out()
coefficients = lr_model.coef_[0]

# Create DataFrame
feature_importance = pd.DataFrame({
    'feature': feature_names,
    'coefficient': coefficients
}).sort_values('coefficient', ascending=False)

# Top positive and negative words
top_positive = feature_importance.head(15)
top_negative = feature_importance.tail(15)

print("🔝 Top 15 Positive Indicators (→ Positive sentiment):")
print()
for idx, row in top_positive.iterrows():
    print(f"   {row['feature']:20s}  coefficient: {row['coefficient']:+.4f}")

print("\n🔻 Top 15 Negative Indicators (→ Negative sentiment):")
print()
for idx, row in top_negative.iterrows():
    print(f"   {row['feature']:20s}  coefficient: {row['coefficient']:+.4f}")
```

# Visualize top features

sections.title: Make Predictions on New Reviews
sections.body:
```python
# New reviews to classify
new_reviews = [
    "This was an amazing film with brilliant acting!",
    "Absolutely terrible. I hated every second of it.",
    "Pretty good movie, though a bit slow at times.",
    "Masterpiece! One of the best films ever made!",
    "Boring and confusing. Complete waste of time.",
]

# Transform and predict
new_reviews_tfidf = vectorizer.transform(new_reviews)
predictions = lr_model.predict(new_reviews_tfidf)
probabilities = lr_model.predict_proba(new_reviews_tfidf)

print("🔮 Predictions on New Reviews:")
print()
for review, pred, proba in zip(new_reviews, predictions, probabilities):
    sentiment = "POSITIVE" if pred == 1 else "NEGATIVE"
    confidence = proba[pred] * 100
    print(f"Review: \"{review}\"")
    print(f"  → Prediction: {sentiment} (confidence: {confidence:.1f}%)")
    print(f"  → Probabilities: Negative={proba[0]:.3f}, Positive={proba[1]:.3f}")
    print()
```

sections.title: Hyperparameter Tuning with GridSearchCV
sections.body:
```python
# Create pipeline
pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('tfidf', TfidfVectorizer(stop_words='english')),
    ('clf', LogisticRegression(random_state=42, max_iter=1000))
])

# Define parameter grid
param_grid = {
    'tfidf__max_features': [300, 500, 1000],
    'tfidf__ngram_range': [(1, 1), (1, 2)],
    'clf__C': [0.1, 1.0, 10.0],
    'clf__penalty': ['l1', 'l2'],
    'clf__solver': ['liblinear']  # Required for l1 penalty
}

# Grid search
print("🔍 Running Grid Search...")
grid_search = GridSearchCV(
    pipeline, param_grid, cv=5, scoring='accuracy', n_jobs=-1, verbose=1
)
grid_search.fit(X_train, y_train)

print("\n✅ Best Parameters:")
for param, value in grid_search.best_params_.items():
    print(f"   {param}: {value}")

print(f"\n🎯 Best Cross-Validation Score: {grid_search.best_score_:.3f}")
print(f"🎯 Test Set Score: {grid_search.score(X_test, y_test):.3f}")
```

sections.title: Compare Different C Values (Regularization)
sections.body:
```python
# Test different regularization strengths
C_values = [0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 100.0]
train_scores = []
test_scores = []

for C in C_values:
    model = LogisticRegression(C=C, random_state=42, max_iter=1000)
    model.fit(X_train_tfidf, y_train)
    train_scores.append(model.score(X_train_tfidf, y_train))
    test_scores.append(model.score(X_test_tfidf, y_test))

# Plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.semilogx(C_values, train_scores, 'o-', label='Training accuracy', linewidth=2)
plt.semilogx(C_values, test_scores, 's-', label='Test accuracy', linewidth=2)
plt.xlabel('C (Regularization parameter)')
plt.ylabel('Accuracy')
plt.title('Effect of Regularization on Model Performance')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("\n💡 Regularization Effect:")
print("   • Low C (strong regularization) → Simple model → May underfit")
print("   • High C (weak regularization) → Complex model → May overfit")
print("   • Sweet spot: Where train and test scores are close!")
```

sections.title: Summary: Logistic Regression for Text
sections.body:
### Key Takeaways
```
1. Fast and interpretable
2. Works great with TF-IDF features
3. Provides probability scores
4. Feature weights show importance
5. Regularization prevents overfitting
```

### Important Parameters
```python
LogisticRegression(
    C=1.0,              # Regularization (smaller = stronger)
    penalty='l2',       # L1 or L2 regularization
    solver='liblinear', # Algorithm (liblinear for small data)
    max_iter=1000,      # Maximum iterations
    class_weight=None   # Handle imbalanced classes
)
```

### When to Use
```
✓ Binary classification (spam, sentiment)
✓ Multi-class classification (topic)
✓ Need interpretability
✓ Need probability estimates
✓ Fast training required
```

### When NOT to Use
```
✗ Complex non-linear patterns
✗ Feature interactions matter
✗ Very deep understanding needed
```

### Next Steps
```
→ Naive Bayes (even faster!)
→ SVM (better for non-linear)
→ Ensemble methods (Random Forest, XGBoost)
```
